headline: Friend detained after youth shot dead in Chattogram
summary: Police detained a 25-year-old's friend after inconsistencies in his statements regarding the shooting in Muradpur-Forest Gate area.
details: A 25-year-old man, identified as Md Azad, was shot dead in the Muradpur-Forest Gate area of Chattogram city this afternoon.
Azad was brought to the Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH) emergency department around 4:00 pm with bullet injuries in his back, where doctors declared him dead.
Police detained Azad's friend, who had brought him to the hospital, after finding inconsistencies in his statements during questioning.
The friend initially claimed that Azad had been shot from behind while walking along a road.
He later changed his story, claiming that he, Azad, and another person were inside an abandoned house in the Forest Gate area consuming yaba when the shooting occurred.
Police visited the location identified by the friend but found no bloodstains, raising further suspicions.
The identity of the friend has not been disclosed by police as the investigation into the killing is ongoing.
caption:
A youth was shot dead in Chattogram, but the friend who brought him to the hospital is now in police custody.

A 25-year-old man, identified as Md Azad, was shot dead in the Muradpur-Forest Gate area of Chattogram city this afternoon.

Azad was brought to the Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH) emergency department around 4:00 pm with bullet injuries in his back, where doctors declared him dead.

Police detained Azad's friend, who had brought him to the hospital, after finding inconsistencies in his statements during questioning.

The friend initially claimed that Azad had been shot from behind while walking along a road.

He later changed his story, claiming that he, Azad, and another person were inside an abandoned house in the Forest Gate area consuming yaba when the shooting occurred.

Police visited the location identified by the friend but found no bloodstains, raising further suspicions.

The identity of the friend has not been disclosed by police as the investigation into the killing is ongoing.

headline: IVACs introduce automatic time slots for Indian visa applications
summary: The new system removes the need for manual slot selection to reduce hassles for applicants across all visa categories in Bangladesh.
details: Indian Visa Application Centres (IVACs) across Bangladesh have introduced an automatic time slot-based system for submitting applications across all visa categories starting July 1, 2026.

Under the new system, time slots will be allotted automatically in a sequential manner based on the daily appointment capacity of each centre, meaning applicants no longer need to manually select a slot.
Applicants are advised to arrive at their respective IVAC as per the time slot provided in their appointment confirmation to ensure a smooth submission process.
This move comes as the Indian High Commission in Bangladesh resumed tourist visas on June 28, nearly two years after they were suspended following political changes in August 2024.
Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi stated that visas are initially being issued through five centres: Dhaka, Rajshahi, Chittagong, Sylhet, and Khulna, with plans to expand further.
Diplomatic sources from the Indian High Commission noted that these improvements aim to reduce hassles for visa seekers and strengthen people-to-people ties between the two nations.
caption:
No more manual slot hunting! Indian visa applications in Bangladesh now feature automatic time-slot allotment.

Indian Visa Application Centres (IVACs) across Bangladesh have introduced an automatic time slot-based system for submitting applications across all visa categories starting July 1, 2026.

Under the new system, time slots will be allotted automatically in a sequential manner based on the daily appointment capacity of each centre, meaning applicants no longer need to manually select a slot.

Applicants are advised to arrive at their respective IVAC as per the time slot provided in their appointment confirmation to ensure a smooth submission process.

This move comes as the Indian High Commission in Bangladesh resumed tourist visas on June 28, nearly two years after they were suspended following political changes in August 2024.

Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi stated that visas are initially being issued through five centres: Dhaka, Rajshahi, Chittagong, Sylhet, and Khulna, with plans to expand further.

Diplomatic sources from the Indian High Commission noted that these improvements aim to reduce hassles for visa seekers and strengthen people-to-people ties between the two nations.
